terms.gloss: as you please, at your discretion
evidence: Plaut. Most. 3.2.106: vīse, spectā tuō arbitrātū (locus in Lewis & Short s.v. arbitrātus; wording not checked)
Lewis & Short s.v. arbitrātus: “freewill, inclination, pleasure” (class.)
terms.comment: The ablative of arbitrātus, one’s own judgement or will: meō arbitrātū, as I like.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 296.
